indicators.note: to overrun something is to spread over and around it, so one word wraps the other

explanation.surface: A raider from the north sweeps across the south-east of England.
explanation.walkthrough: NOR(SE)MAN: the Norman invader takes in SE.
explanation.definitionFit: A Norseman was a medieval Scandinavian seafarer, which is what the term Viking describes.

clue.text: Illegal activity by first army in 1850s' war zone

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Lawbreaking by an advance force in a mid-Victorian conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' simply places one piece beside the next.
explanation.definitionFit: The Crimean War of 1853-56 was fought on the Black Sea peninsula, so the region was its main theatre.

indicators.note: a breaker smashes things apart, so the preceding letters are broken up and reformed

parts.note: the letters of naval and ice, with the tail of the long word serving as the signal

explanation.surface: A navy ship cutting through ice is docked at a Spanish port.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'icebreaker' has to be split: ice is part of the fodder and breaker is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Valencia is a large port city on the eastern coast of Spain.

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns right round, so the following pieces are read backwards

parts.note: a tide of opinion is a trend

explanation.surface: A radical movement within the Catholic faith.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole of TIDE plus RC is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To give credit to a story is to believe it, so credit is trust or belief.

parts.note: a plank is a length of board

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a pirate's victim on a plank; 'On' is the definition, as in on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Aboard means on or onto a ship, train or plane, so it can replace the preposition.

parts.note: the ibis is a long-billed wading bird

explanation.surface: How a big bird protects itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Alibis are pleas of being elsewhere, offered by accused people as excuses or justifications.

indicators.note: novel means new, so the name is given a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Subject matter for a book by Joseph Conrad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a book by the author Conrad, but it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Dacron is a trade name for a polyester fibre used for fabrics, so it is a material.

clue.text: Unit of force giving appearance of weight in light gas

indicators.note: in places one word inside another word

parts.note: neon is a light, inert gas used in lighting

explanation.surface: A physics sentence about something seeming heavy inside a light gas.
explanation.walkthrough: Neon is a 'light gas' both for its use in illuminated signs and for being low in density.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain physics term: the SI measure that accelerates one kilogram by one metre per second squared, honouring Isaac Newton.

clue.text: We're young people, so let's dance madly

indicators.note: madly suggests wild, disordered movement, so the words are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Teenagers announce their youth as a reason to dance wildly.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is spoken by the answer itself, which is why 'We're' sits before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Adolescents are those in the teenage years between childhood and adulthood.

indicators.note: mobile means able to move, so the letters move about

explanation.surface: Describing a slender, agile, flexible body.
explanation.walkthrough: Every surface word sounds like part of the definition; only 'supple' is.
explanation.definitionFit: Lissom describes a body that is thin, graceful and flexible, the same sense as supple.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a thick layer of soft feathers stuffing a duvet or cushion
second meaning: in reality, underneath the outward show

explanation.walkthrough: Down is soft feather stuffing, so 'deep down' read literally is a thick, cosy filling.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means at heart or in truth, whatever the surface suggests; literally it is a generous layer of feathers.

indicators.note: the top of a word in an across entry is its first letter

explanation.surface: A sturdy wooden table with a marble surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm and solid both describe something hard and unyielding to pressure.

indicators.note: behind puts the first-named piece after the second one
the centre of a word is its middle letters only

parts.note: the two middle letters of health

explanation.surface: A garden plot located behind the local clinic.
explanation.walkthrough: An allotment in Britain is a small rented plot for growing vegetables, but here the definition means a share.
explanation.definitionFit: An allotment is a portion handed out, and an allocation is likewise an amount assigned.

clue.text: Submarine was first with rust protection

parts.note: submarine as an adjective means below the sea
to lead is to be in front

explanation.surface: A submarine that came first and was protected against corrosion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Submarine' reads as a noun, a vessel, but it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Underseal is a coating sprayed on a car's underside against corrosion, so an undersealed car has that treatment.

clue.text: Mythical wife evincing regret about early end to game

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so that word is read backwards
end to points to the final letter of the next word only

parts.note: dice is a game of chance

explanation.surface: A legendary wife shows remorse over a game ending too soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'concerning', but it turns the word for regret around; 'early' supplies only its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Eurydice was married to Orpheus, who tried to lead her back from the underworld.

clue.text: Huge portion of sauerbraten or moussaka

indicators.note: a portion is a part taken from a larger whole, so the letters lie within the following words

explanation.surface: A massive serving of German pot roast or Greek baked aubergine.
explanation.walkthrough: Sauerbraten is a German marinated pot roast; moussaka is a Greek dish of aubergine and mince.
explanation.definitionFit: Enormous and huge both describe something of very great size.

clue.text: Place and time for migratory insect

parts.note: a locus is a position or site

explanation.surface: Where and when a swarming insect turns up.
explanation.definitionFit: Locusts are grasshoppers that form vast swarms which travel long distances, devouring crops.

parts.note: the prefix ur- means original or earliest

explanation.surface: A caveman insisting on being seen to at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Something urgent is pressing and calls for prompt action without delay.

clue.text: Talk with heartless lady ? or vice versa

indicators.note: heartless means the middle is cut out, leaving only the outside letters

explanation.surface: Chatting with an unkind woman, or her chatting with you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' simply puts the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Conversely and vice versa both mean with the order or relationship turned the other way.

indicators.note: placed inside says one thing is put within another

parts.note: a vat is another container, a large tank

explanation.surface: A hollow box nested inside a second box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' stands for another container: CAN goes inside VAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Vacant and empty both describe something with nothing or no one in it.

parts.note: a Yank is an informal name for an American

explanation.surface: A shy, introverted editor from the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Withdrawn' looks like shy, but here it means pulled out.
explanation.definitionFit: Yanked means pulled out sharply, so something yanked has been withdrawn or removed.

explanation.surface: A woman's hands meet a painter's approval.
explanation.walkthrough: Ladies' fingers is the British name for the green pod vegetable, not a woman's hands.
explanation.definitionFit: Okra is the tapering green seed pod also known as ladies' fingers or gumbo.

clue.text: Amount given back to younger son to produce wine

indicators.note: something given back returns the way it came, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: a cadet, in older usage, is a younger son of a family

explanation.surface: A sum of money returned to a junior son who makes wine with it.
explanation.walkthrough: Cadet's old sense of a younger son is the one needed here.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscadet is a dry white wine from the Loire valley in western France.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an edition of a magazine
second meaning: something that numbs more, said as NUM-er

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading changes pronunciation: a thing that numbs, with a silent b.
explanation.definitionFit: A magazine's issue is one of its numbers; an anaesthetic is a numbing agent, comically a numb-er.

clue.text: Garments Carthaginian leader introduced to African city

indicators.note: introduced to means brought into, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Tunis is the capital of Tunisia

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so only the initial letter is wanted

explanation.surface: Clothes worn by a Carthaginian general arriving in an African city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carthaginian leader' suggests Hannibal, but only the first letter is wanted; Carthage lay near modern Tunis.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunics are loose garments reaching to the hips or knees, so they are items of clothing.

clue.text: In France I am almost the first priest

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
first asks for only the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A Frenchman claims to be nearly the first clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: JE SUIS loses its final S, then T is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jesuit is a priest belonging to the Society of Jesus, the Catholic order founded by Ignatius Loyola.
